answer.justification: The combination of poorly controlled hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis (elevated bicarbonate) with normal sodium is classic for mineralocorticoid excess. Fatigue and muscle cramps reflect hypokalemia. Primary aldosterone excess (Conn syndrome) explains resistant hypertension despite ACE inhibitor/CCB/diuretic therapy; catecholamine or cortisol excess would have other findings, and impaired renal perfusion is less consistent.
